questions.question: Name the reducing agent in the reaction of KMnO4 with oxalic acid.
steps: The C in H2C2O4 goes from +3 to +4 in CO2, so it is oxidised.
A species that is oxidised is the reducing agent.
Mn is reduced from +7 to +2 by MnO4-, which is the oxidising agent.
So the reducing agent is H2C2O4.

questions.question: Find the volume of water to add to 25.0 cm3 of 1.00 mol dm-3 HCl to make 0.0500 mol dm-3.
Which statement about Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2 is correct?
questions.answer: C: hydrogen ions act as oxidising agents
steps: Mg goes from 0 to +2, so it is oxidised: it is a reducing agent, not an oxidising agent (A is wrong).
H+ goes from +1 to 0 in H2, so it is reduced.
A species that is reduced is an oxidising agent.
So hydrogen ions are oxidising agents, option C.

State the type of reaction in the production of Ca(ClO)2 from Ca(OH)2 and Cl2, justified with oxidation numbers.
questions.answer: Disproportionation: Cl in Cl2 (0) is both oxidised to +1 in Ca(ClO)2 and reduced to -1 in CaCl2.
steps: Cl2 is an element, so Cl = 0.
In Ca(ClO)2 Cl is +1 (O is -2, so Cl = +1); the Cl is oxidised.
In CaCl2 Cl is -1; the Cl is reduced.
The same element is both oxidised and reduced, so it is a disproportionation (a type of redox).

questions.question: Give the reason why chlorine dioxide is not a linear molecule.
questions.answer: The central Cl has a lone pair (and an unpaired electron), so the regions repel and the molecule is bent (about 118 degrees).
steps: Chlorine is the central atom bonded to two O atoms.
It has one lone pair in addition to the bonding regions.
Three electron domains repel to a bent (V) shape rather than 180 degrees.

questions.question: In step 2, compound A disproportionates. Deduce the range of oxidation numbers for Cl in A and justify.
